transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Yeah, so... I came in because lately, since I tried to clean up my image and my whole routine for this arts board stuff, I've just been feeling a lot more tense and, I don't know, down than I expected to be. The arts board is actually super particular, my friend Sarah tried to get involved last year and they completely ghosted her after she submitted her portfolio, which was honestly so rude because she spent like three weeks preparing it and bought this really expensive binder for it. 

But anyway, yeah... since I started trying to get my act together for that, I'm still doing my basic everyday stuff, but I keep dropping all these little things I normally really care about. Like my fair planning notes, or my design drafts. Oh, I was doing this really cool floral design draft last week, trying out this new watercolor technique I saw on TikTok, and I even bought the special brushes for it, but... I don't know, I just stopped. And then I feel so guilty about letting those things slide, and instead of just sitting down and catching up on them, I just end up canceling my plans with people.
Can you tell me more about this feeling of being down? How long have you been feeling this way, and does it seem to happen even when things are going okay in your day?

Um, I'd say it's been going on for about two months now? Yeah, it started right around when I decided to completely overhaul my routine and how I present myself. 

I literally went through my entire closet to try and look more... I don't know, put-together and serious for them. I actually took like three huge garbage bags of my older clothes to the thrift store. Which, by the way, they have this new policy now where they only take donations on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which is honestly so inconvenient. I drove all the way across town on a Wednesday and the guy at the back door wouldn't take them, so I had to just leave the bags sitting in my trunk for a whole extra day. And it made my car smell entirely like old fabric softener. My mom uses that really strong lavender one, and I keep telling her it gives me a headache, but she buys it in those massive bulk jugs at Costco so she refuses to switch to the unscented kind... 

Wait, sorry, I totally lost track of what I was saying. But yeah, it's been about two months since I started that whole routine and presentation overhaul, and that's when this down feeling really started. And it just kind of hangs around, even if I'm just having a normal, okay day where nothing actually goes wrong, you know?
Have you noticed any times when you feel suddenly anxious, panicky, or like your heart is racing for no clear reason?

Um, no, not really. Like, I don't get panicky out of nowhere or anything. I guess my heart only really races if I have, like, way too much caffeine. I used to drink those huge canned energy drinks, but I stopped because they honestly taste like battery acid. 

But last week I went to this new coffee shop over on 4th street—it's super aesthetic inside, they have all these cool neon signs and hanging plants—and I got their seasonal cold brew. It had this salted caramel cold foam on top, which sounded so amazing, but it was honestly way too sweet. Like, sickeningly sweet. And the barista spelled my name completely wrong on the cup. I know my name isn't super complicated, but they somehow put a 'Z' in it? Which makes literally no sense. I actually took a picture of it to send to Sarah because we always joke about how bad coffee shop name spellings are getting. She actually thinks they do it on purpose for free marketing on Instagram, which, honestly, is kind of brilliant if you think about it. Like, people post their misspelled cups all the time and it just gets the brand out there... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the heart racing thing. But yeah, no, I haven't had any sudden panicky feelings or anything like that unless I just drink a ridiculous amount of coffee.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities or hobbies that you previously found interesting or pleasurable?

Um, no, not exactly. Like, I still like doing my art stuff, or at least I want to do it, it's just that I can't seem to get myself to actually sit down and focus on it right now. But I definitely still enjoy it when I do. 

Like, I was actually looking at these new watercolor palettes online the other day. There's this one brand that makes these handmade, super pigmented paints, and they come in these tiny little metal tins. They're gorgeous, but they're shipping from overseas, and the shipping cost is literally more than the paint itself. Which is so frustrating, because I really want to support independent artists, but I can't justify spending forty dollars just on shipping. My friend Sarah ordered some ceramics from a small business in Europe last month, and when the box finally arrived, it looked like it had been kicked all the way across the ocean. Half the mugs were completely shattered. She tried to get a refund, but the post office made her fill out all these complicated forms, and she had to take pictures of the broken pieces from like ten different angles...

But yeah, anyway, I still like my hobbies and stuff. I just feel too tense or guilty to actually do them lately, but the enjoyment is definitely still there.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you're lacking energy, even if you're not doing anything particularly exhausting?

Um, no, I don't think I've been feeling extra tired or anything. I mean, my energy levels feel pretty normal for me. I usually have a decent amount of energy, especially in the mornings. 

Actually, I've been trying to get up earlier lately to catch the sunrise. I saw this TikTok about how getting morning sunlight in your eyes is supposed to reset your circadian rhythm or something? But it's been so cloudy the past few days, so it's kind of just been gray and depressing when I look out the window. Plus, my neighbor has this rooster that crows at literally all hours of the day. I didn't even know you were allowed to keep farm animals in a residential neighborhood. I looked up the city ordinances and apparently, you can have up to six chickens, but roosters are technically banned because of the noise. I've thought about leaving an anonymous note on their door, but I don't want to start some weird neighborhood feud. You know how people get about their pets. My aunt once got into a huge fight with her neighbor over a cat that kept digging in her flower beds, and it got so bad they had to build a taller fence...

Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, being tired. No, I haven't really noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy. Just normal, I guess.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks lately, even when you have the time and energy to do them?

Um, no, my focus has been totally fine. I mean, I don't really have any trouble concentrating on things. If I need to get something done, I can just sit down and do it. 

Like, I was actually hyper-focused the other day organizing my digital photo albums. I had, like, thousands of pictures just sitting on my phone taking up storage space. My phone kept giving me that annoying 'storage full' pop-up every time I tried to take a new picture. I finally decided to back them all up to this cloud service, but the interface was so clunky. I had to drag and drop everything into these specific folders, and it took literally hours. But I found all these old pictures from when my family went to the Grand Canyon when I was in middle school. We drove the whole way there in my dad's old minivan, and the AC broke down somewhere in New Mexico. We had to roll the windows down, but the wind was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio. My brother kept complaining the entire time, and we ended up stopping at this weird roadside diner that claimed to have the world's biggest pancake. It wasn't even that big, honestly, it was just thick. Like a cake. 

But yeah, anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, concentrating. Yeah, no, I haven't had any issues with that. My focus is pretty normal.
Have you noticed any days where you completely lose interest in doing things you normally enjoy, even the things you’ve been talking about like your art or planning events?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I've had any days where I just completely lose interest like that. Like I said, I still really want to do my art and stuff, I just get too wound up about it. But the interest doesn't just vanish. 

Speaking of planning events, though, I was actually supposed to help my cousin plan her baby shower next month. She wants a woodland theme, which I think is so cute, but she's being super picky about the invitations. We spent like three hours at the craft store looking at cardstock. Do you know how many shades of green there are? It's ridiculous. We found this one that was perfect, like a sage green, but they only had twenty sheets left in stock, and we needed fifty. The cashier told us they get their shipments on Tuesdays, but my cousin is convinced they're going to discontinue that specific color before then. She gets so anxious about these little details. I think it runs in the family, honestly. My grandma used to iron her bedsheets because she said wrinkles gave her nightmares. She had this heavy old iron that looked like it belonged in a museum... 

Wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. But no, I haven't noticed any days where I completely lose interest in things.
Have you noticed any days where you feel completely disconnected or indifferent to things you usually care about, like your art or event planning, even if you normally enjoy them?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel disconnected or indifferent. I still care about everything, you know? It's not like I just stop caring about my art or anything like that. 

Actually, I was just looking at my art supplies this morning, thinking I really need to reorganize my markers. I have this huge set of alcohol-based markers—they're supposed to be professional grade, but I swear half of them dried out way faster than they should have. I watched this YouTube tutorial where this girl said you can revive them by injecting rubbing alcohol into the core, but I tried it with one of my favorite blue ones and it just made the ink bleed everywhere. It ruined this whole sketch I was doing of my friend's dog. It's a golden retriever, but he has this weird underbite that makes him look like he's constantly smiling. My friend takes him to this dog park downtown, but apparently, they're closing it next month to build a parking garage. Which is so annoying, because where are people supposed to park when they go to the new farmer's market? They just opened it, and it's already a nightmare trying to find a spot. I went last Saturday and ended up buying this artisanal honey that cost, like, fifteen dollars. It has lavender in it, though, so I guess it's fancy...

Oh, wait, what were you asking? Disconnected? Yeah, no, I definitely still care about things. I haven't felt indifferent at all.
Have you ever felt so down or hopeless that you’ve thought about hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living?

No, no, I've never felt like that. I've never wanted to hurt myself or thought life wasn't worth living. I mean, I get stressed out, obviously, but not like that. 

Though speaking of being stressed out, my roommate was talking about getting a cat to help with her anxiety, and I told her that's a terrible idea right now because our landlord is super strict about pets. He made this huge deal about the people in 3B having a goldfish. A goldfish! He said the tank was a "water damage liability." Can you believe that? Anyway, she wanted to go to the shelter just to look, and we ended up staying there for two hours. They had this one little orange tabby that kept trying to grab my shoelaces through the cage. I was wearing my favorite sneakers, the ones I got on sale last Black Friday. I stood in line in the freezing cold at the mall for like forty-five minutes just to get them. And the guy in front of me kept coughing without covering his mouth, which is just so gross. Like, we just went through a whole pandemic, you'd think people would know how to cough into their elbow by now. I ended up buying hand sanitizer from this kiosk that smelled like synthetic strawberries... 

Wait, sorry. Hopeless? No, I've never felt hopeless or anything like that. I'm okay in that department.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even when you're not feeling particularly stressed or guilty?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I take less pleasure in things. I still really like doing my normal stuff, even when I'm not feeling stressed. I don't think I've lost interest. 

I was actually just thinking about this because I was trying to bake a cake for my neighbor yesterday. She just moved in and she's been so nice, but I realized I didn't have any vanilla extract. So I ran to the grocery store, and you know how they always move things around? I was wandering down the baking aisle for like ten minutes looking for it, and I ran into my old high school gym teacher. It was so weird seeing him outside of school, you know? He was buying three jars of pickles. Like, who needs that many pickles? Unless he's making potato salad or something. My mom makes the best potato salad, but she puts paprika on top, and I always accidentally inhale it and sneeze. She made a huge batch for the Fourth of July last year, and it was so hot outside that the mayonnaise started looking kind of questionable after an hour, so we had to throw half of it away. It was such a waste. 

Oh, right, but no, I still enjoy things just as much as I used to. I haven't noticed any change in that.
Have you had days where you just don't feel like doing anything, even things you usually enjoy, like your art or spending time with friends?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still feel like doing things. I don't just sit around doing nothing. 

Actually, I was just planning a get-together with my friends for this weekend. We're supposed to go to this new escape room that just opened downtown. It's supposed to be pirate-themed, which is kind of cheesy, but my friend Sarah is obsessed with pirates. She even dressed up as Jack Sparrow for Halloween three years in a row. The last year she did it, we went to this party at a warehouse, and the heating was broken, so everyone was freezing. I had to wear my winter coat over my fairy costume, which totally ruined the look. My wings got all bent out of shape in the Uber on the way there, too. The driver was playing this really loud techno music and he had one of those pine tree air fresheners hanging from the rearview mirror, but it didn't smell like pine at all. It smelled more like... I don't know, laundry detergent mixed with cheap cologne? It gave me such a headache. I ended up having to take ibuprofen as soon as we got there, but I couldn't find any water, so I had to swallow it dry, which is the absolute worst feeling. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Days where I don't want to do anything? No, no, I definitely still want to do things. I'm looking forward to the escape room.
Have you noticed that your mood has been low or sad most of the day, more days than not, even if you’re not actively stressed or feeling guilty about something?

No, I wouldn't say my mood is low most of the day. I mean, I get upset sometimes, but not sad all the time. 

Though, speaking of being sad, I was watching this documentary last night about penguins, and it was actually really depressing. They were showing how the ice is melting and this one little baby penguin got separated from its mom. I was sitting there on my couch wrapped in this fleece blanket I got from Target—it's the one with the little geometric patterns on it, you know? They had a whole endcap of them on clearance right after Christmas. I actually went in there just to buy toothpaste, because I ran out and I hate the mint kind, I only like the cinnamon one, but it's so hard to find sometimes. Anyway, the cashier was taking forever because the person in front of me was trying to use a coupon that expired like, two months ago, and they were arguing about it. I was just standing there holding my toothpaste and my blanket, and my phone was at one percent, so I couldn't even scroll through Instagram to pass the time. It's the worst when your phone dies right when you need a distraction. I really need to buy a portable charger, but the good ones are so expensive, and the cheap ones break after like a week. 

But um, no, I'm not sad most days. I feel pretty normal, just, you know, dealing with stuff as it comes.
Have you ever found yourself not really caring about your art or event planning, even when you're not feeling guilty or stressed about it?

No, I don't think so. I still really care about my art and the planning stuff. I mean, it's what I do, you know? 

Actually, I was just looking at some new watercolor paper online this morning because I'm almost out. I usually buy it in bulk from this one specific art supply store, but they were totally sold out of the cold-pressed kind I like. It's so annoying when you have a specific brand you use and suddenly it's just gone. It reminds me of when my favorite coffee shop stopped carrying the oat milk I like. They switched to this cheaper brand that tastes like cardboard, and it totally ruined my morning routine for like a month. I tried going to a different place down the street, but the barista there was always so chatty, and honestly, before 9 AM, I just can't handle small talk. Like, I don't want to explain my weekend plans while I'm waiting for my latte. I just want to pay and leave. Plus, their cups were really flimsy, and one time the lid popped off while I was walking to my car and spilled everywhere. I had to go all the way back inside to get napkins, and it completely ruined my favorite white sweater. I tried everything to get the stain out—baking soda, vinegar, even that expensive stain remover my aunt swears by, but nothing worked. It's still sitting in the back of my closet because I can't bring myself to throw it away. 

But, wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my art. Yeah, no, I still care about it. I definitely haven't lost interest or anything.
Have you had days where your mood has been low or down for most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of two years or more?

No, definitely not two years. I mean, two years is a really long time. I feel like my mood just goes up and down depending on what's happening, you know? 

Like, two years ago, I was actually living in this terrible apartment on the east side of town. The landlord was this grumpy old guy who never fixed anything. The radiator in my bedroom made this horrible clanking noise all winter, and when I complained, he just told me to put a rug over it. Like a rug is going to muffle a metal pipe? I ended up buying this really thick, fluffy area rug from Ikea—the one that looks like fake sheepskin? But my cat, Barnaby, decided it was his new favorite place to throw up hairballs, which was just fantastic. I swear, I was cleaning that thing every other day. I tried switching his food to this expensive grain-free stuff that the vet recommended, but he just turned his nose up at it and went on a hunger strike for three days. Cats are so dramatic. He would just sit by his bowl and stare at me, like I was trying to poison him. I eventually had to mix it with wet food just to get him to eat. The wet food smelled awful, though, like low tide at the beach. Have you ever been to the beach when the tide is out and it just smells like rotting seaweed? I went to Cape Cod once with my family when I was like, twelve, and the smell was so bad I refused to leave the rental house. I just sat inside and watched MTV all week. 

But um, no. Two years of feeling down every day? No, I haven't had that.
Have you ever felt like nothing really interests you anymore, or like you can’t get pleasure out of things you used to enjoy, even for a couple of weeks in a row?

No, not for a couple of weeks in a row. I mean, sure, sometimes I don't feel like doing much, but I wouldn't say nothing interests me or that I don't get pleasure from things. 

Like yesterday, I was actually really excited to try this new recipe I found on Pinterest for lemon blueberry scones. I've been super into baking lately, mostly because it makes the apartment smell good, and I refuse to buy those expensive candles from Bath & Body Works anymore. Did you know they raised the price again? It's ridiculous. I used to go during their semi-annual sale and stock up on the mahogany teakwood ones, but the last time I went, the line was literally out the door. I ended up waiting for like forty-five minutes behind this woman who had a cart full of hand sanitizers. Who even needs that much hand sanitizer? I mean, I guess it's good to be clean, but still. Anyway, the scones turned out okay, but I think I used too much baking powder because they got really puffy and kind of looked like weird little muffins. My friend Sarah came over to try them, and she brought her new dog, which is this tiny little Pomeranian mix that barks at literally everything. It barked at my refrigerator for five minutes straight. I think it saw its reflection or something. Sarah was trying to tell me about her new job at this marketing firm, but I couldn't even hear her over the yapping. She works in downtown now, which sounds like a nightmare for parking. I hate parallel parking. I actually failed my driving test the first time because I hit the cone. The instructor was this really strict guy who sighed loudly every time I checked my mirrors. 

But, um, what was the question? Oh, losing interest in things. No, I still enjoy my baking and stuff. It hasn't been like that for weeks on end.
Have you had days where your mood has been low or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

No, not really. I mean, I've had some bad days lately with all the stress, but not every day for two weeks straight. 

I actually felt pretty good last Tuesday because I finally went to the post office to mail my sister's birthday present. It's always such a hassle going there because the parking lot is tiny, and people just park wherever they want. I ended up having to park next to this huge pickup truck that was practically over the line, and I had to squeeze out of my door like a contortionist. I almost dropped the package, which would have been a disaster because it was this really delicate ceramic vase I found at a flea market. I love flea markets, but you have to go super early to get the good stuff. My friend Jess and I went to one last month, and we got there at like 6 AM. It was freezing, and the only coffee stand there was selling this lukewarm drip coffee that tasted like burnt toast. Jess bought this giant vintage mirror that we barely fit into the back of her hatchback. We had to push the front seats all the way forward, and my knees were basically touching the dashboard the whole ride home. And then we realized the mirror was way too heavy to hang on her apartment wall without finding a stud, so it's just been leaning against her couch for three weeks. Her cat keeps trying to climb it, which is terrifying because it's definitely going to fall and shatter one of these days. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling sad for two weeks. No, it hasn't been like that. Just a day here and there, you know?
Have you ever felt like you can’t get any pleasure out of things you usually enjoy, even for a few days in a row?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing my normal stuff, even if I'm a little stressed. 

Like yesterday, I spent a couple hours organizing my bookshelf by color. I saw it on TikTok and thought it looked so aesthetically pleasing, you know? But it actually took way longer than I thought because I have so many paperbacks with those weird multi-colored spines. And I found this old copy of *The Great Gatsby* that I had to read in high school. My English teacher, Mr. Harrison, was obsessed with that book. He used to wear these really loud, patterned bow ties every single day. I think he owned like fifty of them. One time he wore one with little rubber ducks on it, and the guy sitting next to me—Kevin, I think his name was—kept making quacking noises under his breath the entire period. It was so hard not to laugh. Kevin ended up getting detention because he accidentally knocked over Mr. Harrison's giant Yeti thermos, and coffee went everywhere. It smelled like hazelnut for a week in that classroom. I actually hate hazelnut coffee. It always tastes so artificial, like you're drinking a candle. My mom loves it, though. Every time I visit her, she tries to offer me some, and I have to remind her that I've hated it since I was sixteen. 

But anyway, yeah, I still enjoy things. I still like my books and baking and stuff. So, no, not really.
Have you ever felt like you completely lost interest in things you usually enjoy for at least two weeks in a row?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I think you asked me something like that already, right? But no, not for two weeks straight. 

I actually still really enjoy going to my pottery class on Thursdays. I started taking it a few months ago because I wanted to make my own mugs. I drink a lot of tea, mostly peppermint, and I feel like tea just tastes better in a handmade mug. The instructor is this woman named Brenda who wears these giant, chunky turquoise necklaces and always has clay under her fingernails. She's super nice, but she plays this really weird, slow pan-flute music the whole time. It's supposed to be relaxing, but it honestly just makes me feel like I'm in an elevator at a spa. Last week, I tried to make a bowl, but the clay got totally off-center on the wheel, and it ended up looking like a squished sombrero. Brenda tried to help me fix it, but we just made it worse, so we ended up squishing it back into a ball. The guy next to me, though—I think his name is Greg—he made this perfect, perfectly symmetrical vase on his first try. It was so annoying. He kept talking about how he used to do woodworking, so he has "an eye for form." Like, okay Greg, we get it, you're good with your hands. He also brought in these homemade granola bars to share, which was nice of him, but they were so dry. I took a bite and literally had to chug half my water bottle just to swallow it. It had those weird little dried cranberries in it, and I hate dried fruit in things. It just gets stuck in your teeth. 

Wait, what did you ask again? Losing interest for two weeks? Yeah, no, I still definitely enjoy my pottery and stuff. It hasn't been like that.

Have you ever experienced a period lasting at least two weeks where you completely lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, even things like your art, planning events, or spending time with friends?

I don't think so, no. I mean, didn't you just ask me that? Or maybe it was about feeling sad... I don't know, but no, I haven't lost interest in everything for two weeks. I still like seeing my friends and doing my art projects. 

Actually, I was just planning a get-together for this weekend. My friend Sarah is coming into town, and we haven't seen each other since her wedding last year. Her wedding was beautiful, but it was outdoors in August, which was a terrible idea. It was so humid, my hair completely frizzed out before the ceremony even started. And they had these little paper fans on the chairs, but they didn't do anything. The catering was amazing, though. They had this mashed potato bar where you could put all your own toppings on in a martini glass. I probably ate three glasses of mashed potatoes. Sarah's husband is a chef, so I guess they had to have good food. He works at this fancy Italian place downtown, the one with the string lights on the patio. I went there once for my 21st birthday, and they brought out a giant piece of tiramisu with a sparkler in it. I almost knocked the sparkler into my lap because the waiter startled me when he came up behind me. 

But yeah, anyway, I still enjoy planning things like that. So, no, not for two weeks or anything.
Have you had days where your mood has been low or down for most of the day, more days than not, for a period of at least two years?

No, definitely not for two years. That sounds awful. I mean, I've been feeling kind of stressed lately, but not down for years at a time. 

Actually, two years ago, I was still in school finishing my associate's degree, and that was a really fun time. I lived in this tiny apartment with two roommates, and we had this hideous orange couch that we found on the curb. We cleaned it, obviously, but it always smelled faintly of old pennies. My roommate Jess used to fall asleep on it all the time while watching those true-crime documentaries. I can't watch those, they give me terrible nightmares. Once I watched one about a guy who hid in people's attics, and for a month I made Jess check my closet before I went to sleep. She was such a good sport about it. She's actually moving to Seattle next month for a new job, and I'm supposed to help her pack. I hate packing. You always find so much random junk you forgot you owned. Last time I moved, I found an entire shoebox full of half-used gift cards and old movie tickets. I don't know why I kept them. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't been depressed for two years. Just regular stressed sometimes.

inference_history.note: The patient reports a persistent low mood, increased tension, and loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities for about two months. The symptoms appear to be ongoing regardless of external circumstances, suggesting a possible depressive episode. Additional possibilities include adjustment disorder with depressed mood and generalized anxiety. Further evaluation of symptom severity and functional impairment is needed to narrow the differential.

The patient ruled out concentration difficulties, which reduces support for F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder). However, persistent low mood, guilt, and functional impairment support continued consideration of F32.1 (major depressive episode), F33.1 (recurrent depressive disorder), and F43.22 (adjustment disorder with depressed mood).

The patient continues to report a persistent low mood related to stress and self-imposed expectations around performance and image, but without hallmark features of major depressive disorder such as anhedonia, significant functional impairment, or prolonged low mood nearly every day for at least two weeks. The chronicity of symptoms does not meet criteria for dysthymia (F34.1), but the episodic nature and stressor association support adjustment disorder (F43.22). Major depressive disorder, recurrent mild (F33.1), and single episode mild (F32.1) remain in the differential due to persistent low mood, but the lack of pervasive anhedonia, preserved interest, preserved energy, preserved concentration, absence of hopelessness or suicidal ideation, and episodic rather than pervasive sadness make them less likely. No new disorder is ruled in or out at this turn.

doctor.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

target_item.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
target_item.manifestation: I came in because since I tried to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and down than I expected, like I’m still doing the basics but I keep dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of catching up.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S081) as instructed.

patient.answer:
Um, hi. Yeah, so... I came in because lately, since I tried to clean up my image and my whole routine for this arts board stuff, I've just been feeling a lot more tense and, I don't know, down than I expected to be. The arts board is actually super particular, my friend Sarah tried to get involved last year and they completely ghosted her after she submitted her portfolio, which was honestly so rude because she spent like three weeks preparing it and bought this really expensive binder for it. 

But anyway, yeah... since I started trying to get my act together for that, I'm still doing my basic everyday stuff, but I keep dropping all these little things I normally really care about. Like my fair planning notes, or my design drafts. Oh, I was doing this really cool floral design draft last week, trying out this new watercolor technique I saw on TikTok, and I even bought the special brushes for it, but... I don't know, I just stopped. And then I feel so guilty about letting those things slide, and instead of just sitting down and catching up on them, I just end up canceling my plans with people.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient is experiencing a persistent low mood and diminished interest in activities, which could indicate depression.
doctor.question: Can you tell me more about this feeling of being down? How long have you been feeling this way, and does it seem to happen even when things are going okay in your day?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since I started trying to overhaul my routine and presentation.
target_item.reason: The doctor is explicitly asking 'How long have you been feeling this way', which directly corresponds to the Duration symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
Um, I'd say it's been going on for about two months now? Yeah, it started right around when I decided to completely overhaul my routine and how I present myself.

Brenda tried to help me fix it, but we just made it worse, so we ended up squishing it back into a ball. The guy next to me, though—I think his name is Greg—he made this perfect, perfectly symmetrical vase on his first try. It was so annoying. He kept talking about how he used to do woodworking, so he has "an eye for form." Like, okay Greg, we get it, you're good with your hands. He also brought in these homemade granola bars to share, which was nice of him, but they were so dry. I took a bite and literally had to chug half my water bottle just to swallow it. It had those weird little dried cranberries in it, and I hate dried fruit in things. It just gets stuck in your teeth. 

Wait, what did you ask again? Losing interest for two weeks? Yeah, no, I still definitely enjoy my pottery and stuff. It hasn't been like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of interest in activities they usually enjoy for a significant duration, which is a key symptom for major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced a period lasting at least two weeks where you completely lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, even things like your art, planning events, or spending time with friends?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a two-week period of anhedonia/loss of interest, which is a symptom of Major Depressive Episode. My symptom profile only covers Stress-Related Maladaptive Response (Adjustment Disorder), which does not include a two-week period of anhedonia.

patient.answer:
I don't think so, no. I mean, didn't you just ask me that? Or maybe it was about feeling sad... I don't know, but no, I haven't lost interest in everything for two weeks. I still like seeing my friends and doing my art projects. 

Actually, I was just planning a get-together for this weekend. My friend Sarah is coming into town, and we haven't seen each other since her wedding last year. Her wedding was beautiful, but it was outdoors in August, which was a terrible idea. It was so humid, my hair completely frizzed out before the ceremony even started. And they had these little paper fans on the chairs, but they didn't do anything. The catering was amazing, though. They had this mashed potato bar where you could put all your own toppings on in a martini glass. I probably ate three glasses of mashed potatoes. Sarah's husband is a chef, so I guess they had to have good food. He works at this fancy Italian place downtown, the one with the string lights on the patio. I went there once for my 21st birthday, and they brought out a giant piece of tiramisu with a sparkler in it. I almost knocked the sparkler into my lap because the waiter startled me when he came up behind me. 

But yeah, anyway, I still enjoy planning things like that. So, no, not for two weeks or anything.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent low mood for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years.
doctor.question: Have you had days where your mood has been low or down for most of the day, more days than not, for a period of at least two years?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) symptoms (low mood for at least two years). My symptom profile only covers Adjustment Disorder with symptoms starting within the last few months (Duration: 2 months). Therefore, this symptom is not covered in my profile.

patient.answer:
No, definitely not for two years. That sounds awful. I mean, I've been feeling kind of stressed lately, but not down for years at a time. 

Actually, two years ago, I was still in school finishing my associate's degree, and that was a really fun time. I lived in this tiny apartment with two roommates, and we had this hideous orange couch that we found on the curb. We cleaned it, obviously, but it always smelled faintly of old pennies. My roommate Jess used to fall asleep on it all the time while watching those true-crime documentaries. I can't watch those, they give me terrible nightmares. Once I watched one about a guy who hid in people's attics, and for a month I made Jess check my closet before I went to sleep. She was such a good sport about it. She's actually moving to Seattle next month for a new job, and I'm supposed to help her pack. I hate packing. You always find so much random junk you forgot you owned. Last time I moved, I found an entire shoebox full of half-used gift cards and old movie tickets. I don't know why I kept them. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't been depressed for two years. Just regular stressed sometimes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a mild recurrent depressive episode based on duration (approximately two months), persistent low mood, and functional impairment related to guilt and withdrawal from social plans. The episode is recurrent, as the patient has previously experienced similar depressive episodes, although not meeting criteria for a more severe episode or chronic pattern. No criteria for adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.22) are met due to the internalized nature of the symptoms and lack of a clear, time-limited stressor.
